analysis.title: GS AU & NZ Rates - RBNZ Conway Speech, US October CPI Ahead
key_insights: GIR expects October US core CPI at +0.16% m/m vs +0.2% consensus, consistent with a larger +0.23% core PCE increase in October. BLS interpolation of data missing from last year's government shutdown is expected to add 5bp of residual seasonality to seasonally-adjusted core CPI, boosting public transportation, apparel and hotels.

US rates twist flattened overnight with the long end outperforming. The front end absorbed $58bn of 3y UST, which tailed 0.4bp with low indirect allotment (55.5% vs 63.45% 12-month average). Nasdaq rose 3.5%. Rates came off the cheaps after WTI fell 6% on news Iran may let IAEA inspectors return.

NY sales estimate CTAs covered 10.7mm/bp in the US last week, leaving positioning at 54% of max short. Flows are very bullish and biased to the long end. The long end is 3bp from levels that would intensify buying, and the rest of the curve is about 15bp away.

The NZ curve bear flattened after the election results, which removed the probability of a dual mandate being introduced. Early flows paid December RBNZ and hedge funds unwound front-end longs, then systematic accounts received, mostly in 5-10y IRS.

RBA's Sarah Hunter said AI is adding to demand for stretched construction skills via data centre building, AI price increases are in consumer electronics with small CPI weight, and AI has not yet affected firm headcount nor is expected to over the next year. Australian rates held marginally cheaper.

GS Rates strategy favours tactically paying the February RBA OIS (entry 4.89, target 5.00, stop 4.85) because of the October oil price move and the risk that a hotter inflation print reignites hike risk as inflation expectations begin to shift higher.

GS Rates expects a non-committal RBNZ tightening path to steepen the NZ 2s10s curve as hike premium decays and term premium rises on inflation pressure, macro uncertainty, cyclical risks and looser fiscal policy.

JGB desk sees the super-long sector as rapidly cheap after the futures rally and a buy on relative value. Large flatteners are hard to enter given futures resilience. 40-year bonds look heavy, 30-year repo shorts are about half the prior level, and pension rebalancing demand may be limited, so the 30y auction may tail. Overseas buyers may step in on further steepening.
GBP swaps saw selling of asset swaps and cash, with XCCY bid tracking higher EURUSD. EUR swaps saw fast-money steepening interest. Swedish CTAs continued to receive across the curve.

UK KPMG/REC October jobs report showed renewed contraction in hiring. Permanent placements fell to 46.6 from 50.9, temp billings to 48.9 from 50.9, candidate availability rose to 59.4 from 57.2, vacancies index rose to 48.7 from 48.5 (softest decline since Aug 2024), and permanent salaries rose to 54.1 from 53.4.

GS clients have net sold $30b of tech (TMT + Comm Services) on the US desk since the start of October, $6b of it last week, vs $23b sold during July's momentum drawdown. Friday 11/6 was the first buy-skew day in tech (+$1b) after 7 sessions. Investors are recalibrating datacenter build expectations after the mid-term election, especially in TX and OH. Current prices imply limited y/y capex growth in 2028, well below prior 30-40%+ expectations, which many clients see as an attractive entry point.
